forces.title: Value shifting to invisible control layer and agentic rails in payments
forces.description: Payments value is moving from front-end screens to the invisible control layer of trust, dynamic routing, and agentic rails. This structural shift necessitates market infrastructure entities to invest in back-end trust, machine identity, consent engines, and dynamic routing protocols. Success will depend on operational discipline and technological leadership to capture value in this evolving landscape.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Global payment infrastructure fragmenting regionally, not unifying
forces.description: Instead of converging to a single global standard, payment infrastructure is fragmenting into regional, multi-rail competitive arenas. This forces market infrastructure providers to navigate competing pressures from zero-fee domestic real-time account-to-account (A2A) networks, legacy card perimeters (relevant for UK), and wholesale stablecoin corridors for cross-border settlement, increasing operational complexity and demanding regional orchestration.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI could put up to $160 billion in global payments revenue at risk
forces.description: Agentic artificial intelligence is poised to reshape payments economics, with a potential $75 billion (base case) to $160 billion (aggressive scenario) of global payments revenue at risk by 2030. This poses a significant risk to market infrastructure, as AI agents optimize account yields and dynamically route transactions to minimize fees, impacting deposit net interest income and consumer credit card revenues, particularly in card-heavy markets like the UK.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Digital assets bypassing traditional economics, pressuring infrastructure margins
forces.description: Digital assets such as stablecoins and tokenized deposits present a headwind to traditional payment and deposit revenues. They bypass traditional interchange and foreign-exchange (FX) conversion markups, shifting float income out of commercial bank deposits. As cross-border corporate corridors adopt tokenized settlement, payment infrastructure providers will face direct margin pressure on FX spreads and correspondent banking fees, challenging conventional monetization strategies.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Value shifting from transaction processing to software and workflow layers
forces.description: The true significance of agentic AI lies in its potential to reshape profit pools by shifting value capture from transaction processing scale to software and workflow layers. Market infrastructure providers with deep workflow integration and proprietary interface ownership will command valuation premiums. This transformation requires infrastructure entities to embed payments as a feature of enterprise workflows, moving beyond stand-alone transaction utility.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Accelerating shift to machine-to-machine transactions impacting payment routing
forces.description: Transaction optimization is accelerating its shift to autonomous algorithms, with organizations scaling machine-to-machine applications in B2B and developer-led flows. Machines optimize purely for speed, yield, and fee structure, which will necessitate payment infrastructure to enable dynamic routing capabilities. This displaces traditional human interaction, requiring real-time trust-scoring systems to evaluate machine identity and policy compliance within microseconds.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Displacement of traditional checkout moment into embedded software workflows
forces.description: Three-quarters of interviewed leaders agree that transactions are moving away from dedicated checkout screens and into embedded software workflows. In this model, workflow ownership determines routing. This means market infrastructure needs to adapt to a reality where transactions become a passive consequence of consumption rather than an active decision, requiring integration into diverse software ecosystems and supporting seamless, invisible payments.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Geopolitical and regulatory fragmentation pacing payment rail innovation
forces.description: National supervisory frameworks are viewed as the primary pacing variable for payment rail innovation. Rather than converging, major markets are pursuing paths to preserve monetary sovereignty, leading to supervisory divergence. This fragmentation creates challenges for cross-border payment infrastructure, as it complicates API interoperability and raises questions of legal and financial responsibility for autonomous, cross-border transactions, increasing compliance costs and limiting standardization.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Asymmetric economics of consolidation in payments market
forces.description: Structural consolidation is inevitable in the payments market due to a financial imbalance: IT expenditures compounding at 9% annually versus 4% global payments revenue growth. Massive scale or direct rail control become primary defenses against margin compression for market infrastructure providers. However, this coexists with increasing local fragmentation, making partnerships with domestic payment champions a critical source of competitive advantage, rather than simply fewer operating entities.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Adversarial AI and trust deficit for advanced payment rails
forces.description: Robust fraud mitigation is identified as the ultimate gatekeeper for advanced payment rails. Legacy fraud screening, designed for human interaction, is ineffective against software agents executing transactions in milliseconds. This poses a significant risk for market infrastructure, necessitating the development of real-time trust-scoring systems that evaluate machine identity and policy compliance within microseconds to prevent economically untenable human-in-the-loop dispute resolution.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Opportunity to anchor the emerging trust layer for agentic commerce
forces.description: Autonomous software agents will eventually route transactions dynamically based on cost, speed, and trust, shifting the competitive edge to players enabling agent-directed routing across multi-rail environments. This creates an upside for market infrastructure entities to proactively build positions in the 'trust layer' by establishing protocols for how machines authenticate, consent, and route. Early movers can shape the future of commerce.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Moderating revenue growth from 9% to 4% annually for global payments
forces.description: Global payments revenue growth is moderating from an average annual rate of 9% (2020-2025) to a forecast of 4% (2025-2030), signaling a structural transition. This slowdown, as interest rate tailwinds soften and cash displacement plateaus, means growth will increasingly depend on deliberate competitive advantages rather than broad market momentum. Market infrastructure players must adapt to a lower-growth environment with greater emphasis on efficiency.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Commoditization of cross-border payments execution eroding infrastructure advantages
forces.description: Cross-border payments execution is becoming commoditized, driven by fintech competition and regulatory pushes for transparency and lower costs. Capabilities that once differentiated providers (security, speed, cost) are now table stakes. As traditional rails modernize and new settlement networks emerge, infrastructure-based competitive advantages will steadily erode, forcing market infrastructure players to find new value propositions beyond basic transaction execution.
forces.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

forces.title: Rising compliance costs for distributed cross-border payment ecosystems
forces.description: Compliance complexity is increasing alongside ecosystem complexity, as payments move beyond traditional bank-to-bank networks into interconnected ecosystems involving fintechs and wallet networks. This makes the division of responsibilities for AML, sanctions, and fraud monitoring less straightforward. Managing these distributed obligations raises operational costs for market infrastructure providers, even as customers demand faster, cheaper services, leading to a structural margin squeeze.
forces.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI set to reshape payments economics, posing significant revenue risk by 2030
viewpoints.description: McKinsey projects that agentic artificial intelligence will materially reshape payment economics, potentially putting $75 billion (base case) to $160 billion (aggressive scenario) of global payments revenue at risk by 2030. This risk stems from AI agents optimizing account yields, dynamically routing transactions to minimize fees, and automating purchasing decisions, primarily impacting deposit net interest income and consumer credit card revenues, thus pressuring traditional payment infrastructure profitability.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Digital assets like stablecoins will pose headwinds for traditional payment and deposit revenues
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that digital assets, particularly stablecoins and tokenized deposits, could create headwinds for traditional payment and deposit revenues. These assets bypass traditional interchange and foreign-exchange conversion markups and shift float income away from commercial bank deposits. As cross-border corporate corridors adopt tokenized settlement, payment infrastructure providers will face direct margin pressure on FX spreads and correspondent banking fees, challenging existing revenue models.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: UK market is 'card-resilient' with mature infrastructure, preserving card perimeter dominance
viewpoints.description: McKinsey identifies the United Kingdom, alongside North America and Western Europe, as a 'card-resilient' market. This status is attributed to its mature credit and debit card infrastructure, entrenched merchant acceptance, high-value consumer rewards, and built-in dispute resolution mechanisms. This sustained dominance means automated software agents in the UK are likely to continue routing transactions through established card rails, which remain the default standard for consumer protection and liability management.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Infrastructure battle for agentic commerce demands immediate positioning in trust layer
viewpoints.description: McKinsey stresses that the 'infrastructure battle' for agentic commerce, focusing on how machines authenticate, consent, and route, is currently underway. Financial institutions and payment operators cannot afford to delay, as major networks and tech firms are already drafting emerging agentic protocols. Building positions within this critical 'trust layer' immediately is essential for market infrastructure entities to shape the next era of commerce and enable agent-directed routing across multi-rail environments.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Increasing commoditization of cross-border payment execution, driving margin squeeze
viewpoints.description: McKinsey notes that the cross-border payments industry is experiencing increasing commoditization, with execution becoming a commodity. Competitive pressure from fintechs and regulatory mandates for transparency are driving down costs and making instant settlement the new standard. This leads to a structural margin squeeze for providers, who face rising compliance costs while transaction revenues are pushed downward, requiring a focus on operational excellence.
viewpoints.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

demand_drivers.description: Continued shift from cash to digital payment rails drives transaction volumes.
Payment transaction value grows faster than nominal global GDP.
Providers increase revenue per transaction by embedding software, fraud mitigation, and data services.

pnl_drivers.description: Elevated interest rates drive rapid growth in net interest income (NII); easing rates dampen NII but support fee-based revenues.
Global revenue mix shifting from 46% NII / 54% fee income in 2025 to 44% NII / 56% fee income by 2030 as rates ease.
AI agents could put $75 billion (base case) to $160 billion (aggressive scenario) of 2030 global payments revenue at risk, primarily impacting deposit NII and consumer credit card revenues.

market_sizing.methodology: Total global payments revenue (fee and interest) across all banking activities, before risk cost. Represents 41% of total banking revenues.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

pnl_drivers.driver: Agentic AI Impact on Card Interchange
pnl_drivers.description: Agentic commerce could cut card interchange revenue net of rewards by 30% to 75% in card-heavy markets like the UK. This is due to payment rail substitution, automated repayment optimization, fee avoidance, and real-time foreign-exchange routing by AI agents.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of potential revenue at risk for payments and deposit pools due to agentic AI adoption under various market readiness scenarios. Specific to card-heavy markets like the UK.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world
